title: Differential Longitudinal Patterns of Change Following a Socioemotional Intervention Targeting Empathic Concern and Perspective Taking in Adolescents with Varying Baseline Skills: A Single-Arm Pre–Post–Follow-Up Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Background Empathic concern and perspective taking (ECPT) are relevant to adolescent peer relationships, social motivation, and loneliness. Longitudinal change may differ according to initial ECPT skill level. Objective To examine preliminary longitudinal change following exposure to Flip the Focus , a school-based socioemotional program designed to support ECPT and explore change in social achievement goals and loneliness. Methods Year 9 students from four Australian independent schools were assessed at baseline, 2–3 weeks post-program, and 16 weeks post-program. Linear mixed-effects models included 176 students ( M age = 14.19 years, SD = 0.37; 52.8% female), classified from baseline ECPT z scores as Low ( n = 33), Average ( n = 117), or High ( n = 26). Models examined Time, baseline ECPT group, and Time × Group effects. No contemporaneous untreated comparison was retained. Results ECPT showed a significant Time × Group interaction, ηp² = 0.132: ECPT increased in the Low group, remained stable in the Average group, and declined in the High group before stabilising. Social Development Goals also showed an interaction, ηp² = 0.045, with declines by follow-up in the Average and High groups. Social Demonstration-Avoid Goals showed a smaller interaction, ηp² = 0.032, reflecting a temporary increase in the Low group. Loneliness increased modestly across time without group-specific change. Conclusions Findings provide preliminary evidence of differing longitudinal ECPT trajectories following program exposure. However, baseline-defined ECPT groups are susceptible to regression to the mean, and without a contemporaneous untreated comparison, causal attribution and differential intervention benefit cannot be established. Further controlled evaluation is warranted.
